articles.title: Sunday Summary: Welcome Back, Speyer!
articles.narrative: Tishman Speyer has reacquired the ground lease for the iconic Chrysler Building in New York City, committing $235 million for property improvements. This marks Tishman Speyer's return to ownership of the skyscraper, which it previously held from 1997 to 2008. The deal comes at a time when the Manhattan office market is experiencing strong momentum, with robust consumer spending and high stock market performance contributing to a positive economic outlook for New York's asset-based economy. The new ground lease is set for 150 years, signaling a long-term investment in the historic property.

data_points.address: 405 Lexington Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Iconic, centrally located skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan.
data_points.project_notes: Tishman Speyer previously owned the ground lease from 1997 to 2008. The property was sold in 2019 to RFR Realty for $150 million, but RFR was later pushed out due to missed rent payments and needed improvements. The new ground lease term is 150 years.

articles.market_intelligence: The Manhattan office market is experiencing a historically strong moment, with the volume of available space at its lowest point since 2020. Asking rents are up to $84.56 per square foot on average. The Los Angeles office market is also showing signs of recovery, with L.A. County recording its best quarter for office leasing since 2019, with 4 million square feet of space signed over the summer.
